editions.title: WHO Standard Acupuncture Point Locations in the Western Pacific Region
editions.publisher: World Health Organization, Regional Office for the Western Pacific

source.title: WHO Standard Acupuncture Point Locations in the Western Pacific Region
source.note: Cited by the design proposal. The point count (361) and the proportional-bone (B-cun) method are as the proposal states; the location texts in content/acupoints are paraphrases written without access to the document in this session and must be checked against it.

editions.use: Anatomical location and terminology reference for the 361 meridian points. Not a source of Singapore practice requirements and not a source of safe needling depths.

editions.title: GB/T 12346-2021 Nomenclature and location of meridian points (经穴名称与定位)
editions.publisher: State Administration for Market Regulation / Standardization Administration of China

source.title: GB/T 12346-2021
source.note: Cited by the design proposal for its 362 meridian points. AcuCraft records the commonly reported reason for the difference (Yintang assigned to the Governor Vessel); verify before relying on it.

editions.use: Comparison edition: point identity and codes where it differs from the WHO 2008 standard.

editions.title: A Proposed Standard International Acupuncture Nomenclature

source.title: A Proposed Standard International Acupuncture Nomenclature: report of a WHO Scientific Group
source.note: Source of the EX- codes of extra points (EX-LE2, EX-LE4, EX-HN3, EX-HN5), which the 2008 location standard does not cover.

editions.use: Codes and names of extra points.

differences.summary: Yintang is an extra point (EX-HN3) outside the WHO 2008 standard's 361 meridian points; GB/T 12346-2021 is reported to list it on the Governor Vessel (GV29), which accounts for its 362 points.
